title: Bookmark Manager Core
description:
Build core bookmark management functionality for the Python Bookmark CLI.

## Goals
- Users can add bookmarks with URL and optional title
- Users can list all saved bookmarks
- Users can delete bookmarks by ID

## Success Criteria
- User can add a bookmark with URL and optional title
- User can list all bookmarks with ID, title, and URL
- User can delete a bookmark by ID
- Bookmarks persist across runs in bookmarks.json

## Out of Scope
- Tags or categories
- URL validation/fetching
- Browser integration

title: Add and view bookmarks
description:
Users can add new bookmarks and view all saved bookmarks.

## User Stories
- As a user, I can add a bookmark so I can save URLs for later
- As a user, I can list bookmarks so I can see what I've saved

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `python3 bookmark.py add <url>` saves a bookmark
- [ ] `python3 bookmark.py add <url> --title "Name"` saves with custom title
- [ ] `python3 bookmark.py list` shows all bookmarks with ID, title, and URL
- [ ] Bookmarks without explicit title use the URL as title
- [ ] Data persists in bookmarks.json across runs

## Technical Notes
- BookmarkManager class in bookmark.py
- argparse for CLI with subcommands
- JSON file persistence
- unittest for tests

title: Implement data model and add command
description:
Create the BookmarkManager class with data model and implement the add and list commands.

## Requirements
- BookmarkManager class in bookmark.py with add() and list_bookmarks() methods
- `python3 bookmark.py add <url>` saves a bookmark
- `python3 bookmark.py add <url> --title "Name"` saves with custom title
- `python3 bookmark.py list` prints all bookmarks with ID, title, and URL
- Each bookmark: {id, url, title, created_at}
- IDs: first 8 chars of uuid4
- Persistence: load/save bookmarks.json
- Missing URL rejected with error message
- Bookmarks without explicit title default to the URL

## Implementation Notes
- Use argparse with subcommands
- BookmarkManager.__init__ loads from JSON file, creates empty list if missing
- save() writes to bookmarks.json after each mutation
- list output format: `[id] title (url)`

## Test Specifications

### Unit Tests (test_bookmark.py)
- test_add_bookmark_creates_item_with_correct_fields
- test_add_bookmark_uses_url_as_default_title
- test_add_bookmark_with_custom_title
- test_list_bookmarks_returns_all_items
- test_persistence_survives_reload

### Manual Verification
- python3 bookmark.py add "https://example.com" → prints confirmation
- python3 bookmark.py add "https://python.org" --title "Python" → prints confirmation
- python3 bookmark.py list → shows both bookmarks
- Restart and list again → bookmarks still there

title: Implement list command formatting
description:
Enhance the list command with numbered output and empty-state messaging.

## Requirements
- `python3 bookmark.py list` shows numbered bookmarks
- Output format: `1. [id] title (url)`
- Empty state prints: "No bookmarks saved yet."
- Bookmarks sorted by creation date (newest first)

## Dependencies
- Requires demo-001.1.1 (data model and add command)

## Implementation Notes
- Modify list_bookmarks() to sort by created_at descending
- Add numbered output formatting
- Handle empty bookmarks list gracefully

## Test Specifications

### Unit Tests (test_bookmark.py)
- test_list_empty_returns_message
- test_list_shows_numbered_output
- test_list_sorted_newest_first

### Manual Verification
- python3 bookmark.py list (empty) → "No bookmarks saved yet."
- Add 2 bookmarks, list → shows numbered, newest first

title: Manage bookmarks
description:
Users can delete bookmarks they no longer need.

## User Stories
- As a user, I can delete a bookmark so I can remove URLs I no longer need

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `python3 bookmark.py delete <id>` removes a bookmark
- [ ] Invalid ID prints error message
- [ ] Deletion persists in bookmarks.json

## Technical Notes
- Builds on BookmarkManager from demo-001.1.1
- ID matching uses prefix match (user can type first few chars)

title: Implement delete command
description:
Implement the ability to delete bookmarks by ID.

## Requirements
- `python3 bookmark.py delete <id>` removes a bookmark
- ID matching: prefix match (user can type first few chars)
- Invalid ID prints error message
- Deletion persists in bookmarks.json
- Prints confirmation with deleted bookmark title

## Dependencies
- Requires demo-001.1.1 (data model and add command)

## Implementation Notes
- Add delete() method to BookmarkManager
- Match by ID prefix, error if no match or ambiguous
- Remove from list and save

## Test Specifications

### Unit Tests (test_bookmark.py)
- test_delete_removes_bookmark
- test_delete_persists_state
- test_delete_invalid_id_raises
- test_delete_prefix_match

### Manual Verification
- python3 bookmark.py add "https://example.com" → note the ID
- python3 bookmark.py delete <id> → prints confirmation
- python3 bookmark.py list → bookmark gone
- Restart and list → still gone

title: Search & Export
description:
Add search and export capabilities to the bookmark manager.

## Goals
- Users can search bookmarks by keyword
- Users can export bookmarks to JSON format

## Success Criteria
- User can search bookmarks by keyword matching title or URL
- User can export all bookmarks to a formatted JSON file
- Search results display matching bookmarks clearly

## Dependencies
- Requires core bookmark functionality (demo-001) to be usable

title: Search bookmarks
description:
Users can search saved bookmarks by keyword.

## User Stories
- As a user, I can search bookmarks so I can find specific URLs quickly

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `python3 bookmark.py search <keyword>` finds matching bookmarks
- [ ] Search matches against both title and URL
- [ ] Case-insensitive matching
- [ ] No results prints: "No bookmarks matching '<keyword>'."

## Technical Notes
- Builds on BookmarkManager from demo-001
- Simple substring matching (no regex)

title: Search by keyword
description:
Implement keyword search across bookmark titles and URLs.

## Requirements
- `python3 bookmark.py search <keyword>` finds matching bookmarks
- Matches against both title and URL fields
- Case-insensitive substring matching
- Output format same as list (numbered)
- No results: "No bookmarks matching '<keyword>'."

## Dependencies
- Requires demo-001.1.1 (data model) — cross-epic dependency

## Implementation Notes
- Add search() method to BookmarkManager
- Filter bookmarks where keyword appears in title or URL (case-insensitive)
- Reuse list formatting for results

## Test Specifications

### Unit Tests (test_bookmark.py)
- test_search_finds_by_title
- test_search_finds_by_url
- test_search_case_insensitive
- test_search_no_results_message

### Manual Verification
- Add bookmarks with different titles/URLs
- python3 bookmark.py search "python" → finds matching ones
- python3 bookmark.py search "PYTHON" → same results (case-insensitive)
- python3 bookmark.py search "zzzzz" → "No bookmarks matching 'zzzzz'."

title: Export bookmarks
description:
Users can export bookmarks to a JSON file.

## User Stories
- As a user, I can export my bookmarks so I can back them up or share them

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `python3 bookmark.py export [filename]` writes bookmarks to a JSON file
- [ ] Default filename: bookmarks_export.json
- [ ] Export format is pretty-printed JSON
- [ ] Prints count of exported bookmarks

## Technical Notes
- Builds on BookmarkManager
- Depends on search being implemented first (to verify data model is stable)

title: Export to JSON
description:
Implement export of bookmarks to a JSON file.

## Requirements
- `python3 bookmark.py export` writes to bookmarks_export.json
- `python3 bookmark.py export output.json` writes to specified file
- Export format: pretty-printed JSON array of bookmark objects
- Prints: "Exported N bookmarks to <filename>."
- Empty bookmarks: "No bookmarks to export."

## Dependencies
- Requires demo-002.1.1 (search) to verify data model stability

## Implementation Notes
- Add export() method to BookmarkManager
- Use json.dump with indent=2
- Accept optional filename argument via argparse

## Test Specifications

### Unit Tests (test_bookmark.py)
- test_export_creates_file
- test_export_default_filename
- test_export_custom_filename
- test_export_empty_bookmarks_message
- test_export_content_matches_bookmarks

### Manual Verification
- Add a few bookmarks
- python3 bookmark.py export → creates bookmarks_export.json
- python3 bookmark.py export my_bookmarks.json → creates custom file
- cat bookmarks_export.json → pretty-printed JSON

title: Consider tag support for bookmarks
description:
Evaluate adding tags/categories to bookmarks for organization.

## Research Topics
- Tag data model (list of strings per bookmark)
- CLI syntax for adding tags: --tags "python,tutorial"
- Filtering by tag: `bookmark.py list --tag python`
- Tag-based search vs keyword search

## Why This is Parked
Simple URL storage is sufficient for MVP. Tags add UI complexity and data model changes.

## When to Revisit
- If users have many bookmarks and need organization
- If keyword search proves insufficient
- After core features are stable
